name: Mecca
tagline: The holiest city in Islam, for Hajj and Umrah
summary: The birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and the direction of prayer for Muslims everywhere. Millions come each year for Umrah, and for Hajj in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Only Muslims may enter the city; non-Muslim travellers can learn about it in Jeddah and Medina's museums.
seasonNote: Hajj dates move about 11 days earlier each year with the Islamic calendar; Ramadan, especially the last ten nights, is the busiest time for Umrah. Summer passes 45°C.
arrival: Only Muslims may enter Mecca; checkpoints on every road enforce this. Fly to Jeddah, then take the Haramain high-speed train (about 35 minutes) or a bus. Umrah is booked through the official Nusuk app; Hajj needs a Hajj visa through an authorised operator or your country's quota.
gettingAround: Most hotels are walking distance from the Grand Mosque; buses and the Mashaer metro (during Hajj) serve the holy sites at Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafat.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry riyals for small shops and taxis.
foodTip: Eat simply between prayers: Al Baik fried chicken, mandi rice with lamb, and Zamzam water, which is free throughout the mosque.
buyTip: Prayer mats, misbaha prayer beads, perfume oils, dates and Zamzam water in sealed containers for home.
baseArea: The hotels around the Grand Mosque, especially the Abraj Al-Bait towers and Ibrahim Al Khalil Road

connections.note: Flights land in Jeddah, then the train to Mecca.

items.name: Masjid al-Haram and the Kaaba
items.summary: The Great Mosque surrounding the Kaaba, the centre of Muslim worship, where pilgrims perform tawaf and sa'i.
items.expect: Muslims only; huge crowds at prayer times and in Ramadan; ihram clothing is required for Umrah.
items.tip: Perform tawaf late at night or after Fajr for the calmest time; the upper floors are less crowded.

items.name: Jabal al-Nour and the Cave of Hira
items.summary: The mountain cave where the Prophet received the first revelation of the Quran.
items.expect: A steep climb of about 1,200 steps, an hour or more; very hot by day.
items.tip: Start before dawn with water and a torch; the Hira Cultural District at the foot explains the story.

items.tip: Many Umrah pilgrims visit Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafat on a guided ziyarah tour.
